text: do these findings affect treams-rs and advect?

items.html:
The first two apply to both repositories. The newer findings need qualification:

Finding treams-rs Advect
Old extension-module wiring Applies: native manifest Applies: native manifest
clippy::all = warn weakens defaults Applies: workspace lint Applies: workspace lint
Two build commands can collapse Yes, in sdist CI: workflow Yes, in sdist CI: workflow
Hypothesis inherits CI health-check suppression Yes, with intentional CI inheritance: profiles No: explicitly uses the built-in default parent

The practical changes and boundaries:

  • PyO3: treams-rs locks 0.29.3, Advect 0.29.2. Both require Maturin ≥1.12, so the feature declaration and its tool.maturin.features activation can go. Their sole workspace feature then disappears, making the lint command’s --all-features redundant. This matches PyO3’s guidance.
  • Clippy: remove the all = …warn entry. That restores deny-by-default correctness lints while retaining the other configured groups. Both CI commands already use -D warnings, so CI enforcement remains effective. Clippy documentation
  • Builds: plain uv build already builds the wheel from the sdist. Both CI sequences can collapse, with output-path adjustments and existing artifact/smoke checks preserved. treams-rs’s local check-wheel already has only one build. Avoid substituting uv build --sdist --wheel: that builds both directly from source. uv documentation
  • Hypothesis: I reproduced treams-rs’s behavior under simulated CI: all three profiles inherit derandomize=True, database=None, and suppression of HealthCheck.too_slow, which checks input-generation speed. Its comments deliberately describe the first two settings; the suppression is the additional consequence. Advect’s profiles retain no suppressed health checks in either environment. I would make treams-rs’s health-check choice explicit, preserving its intended CI policy. Hypothesis settings

Verified configuration, upstream guidance, and effective Hypothesis profiles. No package builds or full test suites run; no repository changes made.

text: ok i want you to fully address and fix all of this, we want everrything to be clean and strict. open prs in both repos and babysit them through merge. decide whether or not this requires/justifies a release for either package and act accordingly. the goal is for everything to be done. you dont need to ask for my permission
make sure to adversarially review your own changes too
when youre done with everything, explain the changes to me and whether there were any effects on the codebases

items.html:
Everything is complete and merged:

  • treams-rs #4
  • Advect #47
  • Advect #48, covering an additional development-tooling security issue found during the final audit.

The changes and their effects:

  • PyO3: Removed obsolete extension-module feature wiring. Both projects now rely on Maturin’s existing configuration. Wheel building and native Rust tests passed.
  • Clippy: Removed all = "warn", restoring correctness lints to errors locally. CI already treated warnings as errors, so this makes local behavior stricter.
  • Packaging: Replaced redundant build commands with one uv build, which builds the sdist and then its wheel. Archive validation and installed-wheel smoke tests remain.
  • Hypothesis: Enabled all health checks explicitly in treams-rs’s development, CI, and thorough profiles, while preserving their intended budgets and reproducibility settings. Advect already handled inheritance correctly.
  • Advect security: Updated development-only virtualenv and python-discovery, and fixed the uv requirement that blocked Dependabot. All four security alerts automatically closed as fixed.

Neither codebase’s numerical implementation, public API, or runtime dependency graph changed. The practical effects are stricter checks, simpler builds, and patched development tooling. Advect now requires uv>=0.12.18,<0.13; your global uv remains 0.12.3, while validation used an isolated compatible version.

Five adversarial review passes found no remaining actionable issues. Local tests, fresh package builds and installations, PR checks, and both repositories’ final main-branch CI passed. Performance benchmarks and release-publication workflows were not run.

No release was warranted or published: these changes affect repository tooling and tests. Published versions remain treams-rs 0.1.1 and Advect 0.3.0.

All changes were pushed and merged, PR descriptions updated, and no PR comments posted. Both local main checkouts are clean and current; temporary worktrees, branches, and tooling were removed.
